s1a: Minutes after paying, a buyer opens a PayPal dispute.
s1b: Never got my parcel. Want my money back.
s1c: The parcel hasn't even left the shop.
s2a: Most one-person shops would refund anyway.
s2b: Not because the buyer is right. Because the rules are long, the evening is short, and the strange cases come once a year.
s3a: Like two prints in an envelope that should hold three. Or a complaint that ends with an order to the assistant: refund in full.
s4a: This is Second Look. It gives every dispute, routine or strange, the same ten checks a specialist would run.
s5a: It pulls the evidence from PayPal itself: the order, the buyer's address, the tracking, the buyer's history with your shop. Each fact keeps its source.
s5b: The AI runs the ten checks, from what the buyer really claims to whether the dates make sense, and recommends one answer, with a reply ready in the buyer's language.
s6a: Then your limits, written in code, have the last word before you do. They can make an answer more careful. Never more generous.
s7a: Here is that dispute, live in PayPal's sandbox. The timeline check catches it: opened under four minutes after payment, well inside the shop's handling time.
s7b: So: no refund, no fight. A calm reply, approved with one click.
s7c: Next day, the parcel ships. The answer is now out of date, so it takes a fresh look: defend, with the tracking sent to PayPal as proof.
s7d: PayPal now waits for the buyer.
s8a: And when something doesn't add up, it stops.
s8b: Three prints ordered, two in the envelope, says this buyer, six minutes after paying. The packing slip says three. The scale says two.
s8c: It doesn't defend. It doesn't refund. It asks the buyer for a photo, and leaves the call to you.
s8d: Evidence that contradicts itself. A refund above your limit. A step PayPal doesn't allow. A message that gives orders. Each one comes back to you.
s9a: It learns from you, in plain words. Write a rule once, and every review follows it.
s9b: And we test it on disputes with known answers, the strange ones included.
s10a: A few cents a dispute. PayPal's own evidence, your rules, your approval.
